candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Exodus
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Exodus XV.1 (NPNF S2 V13, Gwynn/Schaff trans., Oxford 1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Exodus (c. 360 AD)

'I will sing unto the Lord, for he hath triumphed gloriously' — the first canonical hymn of victory, sung on the shore of the sea by the redeemed. Ephrem treats Ex 15:1 as the prototype of all Pascal hymnody: every Easter song of the Church is a continuation of Moses' shore-song. Tewahedo mäzmur-tradition recognizes the Song of Moses among its earliest canonical warrants for hymnic praise after deliverance.

candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Hymns on the Crucifixion
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Hymns on the Crucifixion VIII.4 (NPNF S2 V13). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Hymns on the Crucifixion (c. 365 AD)

The Lord shows Moses a tree, and the tree cast into the bitter waters of Marah makes them sweet. Ephrem reads the wood as the Cross before its time: what sweetens the waters of the world is the wood of the Cross cast into them. Tewahedo Holy-Week catechesis cites Ex 15:25 as one of its principal OT cross-typology anchors.
